days.title: Everything Is by Decree
days.question: What does it mean to believe in the divine decree? Did Allah write everything before it happens?
days.principle: We believe in the divine decree, its good and its bad, from Allah the Exalted: believing that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, that He wrote everything in the Preserved Tablet, that His will is carried out in everything, and that He alone is the Creator of everything.
days.action: When something happens to you today that is not to your liking, remember the hadith «لو اجتمعوا على أن يضروك بشيء لن يضروك إلا بشيء قد كتبه الله عليك», and say: «قدر الله وما شاء فعل».
lesson: Belief in the divine decree is one of the pillars of faith. It means believing that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, that Allah wrote everything in the Tablet, that His will is carried out in everything, and that He alone is the Creator of everything. The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah wrote the measures of all creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. He also taught us that if the whole Ummah gathered to benefit or harm you, they could only do so with what Allah has written. Even incapacity, intelligence and skill are by decree. This belief gives the heart tranquillity, as the verse says: ﴿قُل لَّن يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَنَا﴾.

quiz.question: A calamity befell you and you are worried that someone caused it. What is the correct understanding of the decree?
options: People can harm you with something Allah did not write
Everything happens by chance
The decree is only for big things
No one can harm you except with something Allah has written for you

quiz.question: When were the measures of creation written?
options: At the moment the event happens
After the person does the act
Before the creation of the heavens and the earth
They are not written at all

quiz.question: What does belief in the decree include?
options: That Allah only knows, without writing
Allah's knowledge of everything, His writing it, His will being carried out, and His creating everything
That Allah wrote only the good
That people do everything without Allah's will

askTheBook: What does belief in the divine decree mean?
When did Allah write the measures of creation?
What does "the pens have been lifted and the pages have dried" mean?

days.title: Two Groups Went Astray About the Decree
days.question: If Allah has written everything, am I forced? Or am I completely free and there is no decree?
days.principle: Two groups went astray regarding the decree: one denied the decree entirely, and their view ultimately attributes ignorance and incapacity to Allah; the other denied human will entirely, and their view ultimately attributes injustice to Allah. Allah is far exalted above that.

misconception.peopleSay: A human is like a feather in the wind; he has no choice in what he does.
misconception.correct: This is the view of the group that denied human will entirely, equating what befalls a person involuntarily with what he does by choice. Their view ultimately attributes injustice to Allah, as if He holds His servants accountable for what they have no hand or choice in. Allah is far exalted above that.

days.action: Today, distinguish between something that happened to you against your will and something you chose to do by your own will, and remember that the book says confusing the two is the error of the second group.
lesson: The book explains that two groups erred on the decree. The first denied the decree altogether and said Allah does not know a thing until after it happens, which ultimately attributes ignorance and incapacity to Allah. When Ibn 'Umar heard about them, he declared himself free of them and said that Allah would not accept from them even if they spent the like of Mount Uhud in gold until they believed in the decree. The second group denied human will altogether and said a person is like a feather in the wind, which ultimately attributes injustice to Allah, holding people accountable for what they had no choice in. The polytheists themselves said, "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated partners," and Allah answered that this is a false argument, because He sent them messengers forbidding them.
days.quote: There is no one among people except that he wills what he does not do or does what he does not will; but Allah alone does whatever He wills.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Allah doesn't know what I will do until I do it." What does this view lead to?
options: Attributing ignorance and incapacity to Allah, which is misguidance
A correct understanding of freedom
It has no problem at all
This is the view of Ahl as-Sunnah
quiz.explanation: The view of this group ultimately attributes ignorance and incapacity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

quiz.question: Someone says: "I'm forced in everything; I have no choice." What does this view lead to?
options: This is the correct understanding of the decree
It has no problem at all
It really does free him from accountability
Attributing injustice to Allah, as if He holds people accountable for what they had no choice in
quiz.explanation: And a group denied human will entirely.

quiz.question: If people were forced, why did Allah send messengers and punish the nations that denied them?
options: That was without wisdom
The messengers had no purpose
Because a human has choice and is held accountable for it
The punishment was random
quiz.explanation: Allah sent them His messengers, and made them taste His punishment.

askTheBook: Which groups went astray regarding the decree?
How did the polytheists argue from Allah's will, and how did Allah answer them?
What did Ibn 'Umar say about those who denied the decree?

days.title: The Middle Way on the Decree
days.question: How do I reconcile that Allah wills everything with the fact that I have a choice and will be held accountable?
days.principle: Ahl as-Sunnah affirmed the decree with its four levels: knowledge, writing, will and creation. They distinguished between Allah's universal will and His legislative will, and affirmed that the servant has a will and the ability to choose, encompassed by Allah's power and governed by His will.

misconception.peopleSay: I commit sins because Allah wrote them for me, so it's not my fault.
misconception.correct: Something close to this doubt has spread among many sinners and negligent people who use the decree as an excuse for their negligence. It is well known that the decree is not used as an excuse for faults; rather, one finds consolation in it when calamities strike.

days.action: Supplicate today with the Prophet's ﷺ supplication: «اللهم مصرف القلوب صرف قلوبنا إلى طاعتك».
lesson: Ahl as-Sunnah stood in the middle between the two groups and affirmed the decree with its four levels: knowledge, writing, will and creation. They distinguished between the universal will, meaning what Allah wills to happen in the universe, and the legislative will, meaning what Allah loves and commands. So disbelief can occur in the universe by Allah's universal will, but He is not pleased with it and does not love it. They also affirmed that a person has a will and an ability to choose, but not an absolute one; it lies within Allah's will. Moral responsibility is tied to reason, ability and the proof reaching a person, so the insane, the coerced, and the ignorant person who is unable to learn are not accountable. Allah has not punished anyone until after sending him a messenger, and that is from His justice.
days.quote: And that the basis of moral responsibility consists of reason, ability and the proof having reached a person.

quiz.question: Someone commits sins and says: "Allah wrote them for me." Can he use the decree as an excuse like this?
options: Yes, since they are written it isn't his fault
No, the decree is for patience in calamities, not an excuse for sins
Yes, if that's how he feels
Only for minor sins
quiz.explanation: Something may happen in Allah's dominion that He does not will legislatively and is not pleased with, such as disbelief and shirk.

quiz.question: A small child made a mistake. Is he held accountable for it?
options: No, the pen is lifted from the child until he reaches puberty
Yes, exactly like an adult
He is half accountable
His parents are held accountable instead

quiz.question: What are the conditions for a person to be morally responsible and accountable?
options: Wealth and health
Old age only
Having studied religious knowledge
Reason, ability and the proof having reached him
quiz.explanation: And that the basis of moral responsibility consists of reason, ability and the proof having reached a person.

askTheBook: What are the levels of the decree according to Ahl as-Sunnah?
What is the difference between the universal will and the legislative will?
From whom is moral responsibility lifted?

days.title: Faith: Word, Deed and Belief
days.question: Is faith just believing in my heart, or does it also require action?
days.principle: Faith is word, deed and belief; it increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience. Its foundation is affirming what Allah has told and submitting to the Shariah; whoever lacks affirmation and submission in his heart is not a Muslim.

misconception.peopleSay: As long as I believe in my heart that Islam is true, I'm a believer, even if I don't submit to any ruling.
misconception.correct: Faith is not achieved merely by believing that the Prophet ﷺ is truthful in what he brought; many people had that and did not become believers by it. Two things must come together: believing in his truthfulness, and the heart's love and submission.

days.action: Think of one thing you believe is part of the religion but don't do, and start it today so that your belief is accompanied by submission.
lesson: For Ahl as-Sunnah, faith is not just a word; it is word, deed and belief, increasing with obedience and decreasing with disobedience. The foundation of faith is two things together: affirming what came from Allah, and submitting to the Shariah. Those who removed deeds from faith entirely and said it is only affirmation are mistaken, because many people affirmed the truth and did not become believers. At the same time, those who included all deeds in the foundation of faith went to excess, because the Shariah distinguished between deeds whose loss removes faith and deeds whose loss only reduces its completeness. Pharaoh's people were certain of the signs within themselves but denied them out of injustice and arrogance. And the scholars of the People of the Book knew the Prophet ﷺ as they knew their own sons, yet they concealed the truth.
days.quote: Guidance is achieved only through knowledge, affirmation, humble devotion and submission.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Faith is in the heart; it doesn't matter whether I do anything." What is the correct understanding?
options: He is right, faith is only in the heart
Faith is only words on the tongue
Faith is word, deed and belief; it increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience
Faith is fixed, neither increasing nor decreasing
quiz.explanation: We believe that faith is word, deed and belief; it increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience.

quiz.question: Someone believes the Prophet ﷺ is truthful but refuses to follow or submit to him. Is he a believer?
options: Yes, affirmation is enough
No, affirmation must be joined by the heart's love and submission
Yes, if his heart is good
A believer who falls short
quiz.explanation: Rather, two things must come together: believing in his truthfulness, and the heart's love and submission.

quiz.question: Someone knows the truth in his heart, but his words and actions contradict it. Is that knowledge faith?
options: No, knowledge in the heart alone is not faith if words and deeds contradict it
Yes, knowledge is faith
Yes, as long as he is convinced
Complete faith
quiz.explanation: Knowledge in the heart alone is not faith if words and deeds contradict it.

askTheBook: What does it mean that faith is word, deed and belief?
Is affirmation alone enough for me to be a believer?
What is the difference between the foundation of faith and its completeness?

days.title: People of Major Sins Are Subject to Allah's Will
days.question: If a Muslim commits a major sin, does he leave Islam?
days.principle: A Muslim does not become a disbeliever unless he nullifies his faith with shirk, and he does not become a disbeliever by committing major sins unless he regards them as lawful. People who commit major sins are subject to Allah's will: if He wills He punishes them, and if He wills He forgives them.

misconception.peopleSay: Anyone who commits a major sin has left Islam, period.
misconception.correct: A Muslim does not become a disbeliever by committing major sins unless he regards them as lawful. People of sins less than shirk are subject to Allah's will: if He wills He punishes them, and if He wills He forgives them, and on the whole they remain within the circle of Islam.

days.action: If you fall into a sin, do not despair or think you have left the religion; remember the verse ﴿وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ﴾ and hasten to repent.
lesson: Faith increases; the Quran says Allah sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers so that they would increase in faith along with their faith. The Prophet ﷺ told us that some people will come out of the Fire with an atom's weight of faith in their hearts. Then the book establishes that a Muslim does not become a disbeliever through a major sin unless he regards it as lawful, and that people of major sins are subject to Allah's will. The verse distinguished between shirk, which Allah does not forgive, and what is less than it, which He may forgive for whom He wills, even without repentance. The Prophet ﷺ distinguished between sinfulness and disbelief, and said that his intercession is for the people of major sins in his Ummah, which proves they are still within the circle of faith. The Shariah also set different punishments for sins, which proves that sins are not all of one level.
days.quote: And his ﷺ intercession for them is proof that they remain within the circle of faith.

quiz.question: A Muslim committed a major sin such as theft, knowing it is haram. What is his ruling?
options: A disbeliever who has left Islam
A Muslim with no sin at all
A hypocrite
He does not become a disbeliever; he is a sinner subject to Allah's will
quiz.explanation: And that he does not become a disbeliever by committing major sins unless he regards them as lawful.

quiz.question: The Shariah made the punishment for theft different from that for zina, for drinking alcohol and for apostasy. What does this difference teach us?
options: That all sins take one out of Islam
That punishments are at the judge's discretion with no rule
That sins have ranks and are not all of one level
That all sins are equal before Allah
quiz.explanation: And in that is proof that sins differ in rank and are not all of one level.

quiz.question: Are all sins of one level?
options: Yes, all are disbelief
No, there is sinfulness and there is disbelief, and sins are not equal
Yes, all are minor
There is no difference between one sin and another
quiz.explanation: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distinguished between sinfulness and disbelief, from which it is known that sins are not equal.

askTheBook: Does a Muslim become a disbeliever through a major sin?
What does it mean that people of major sins are subject to Allah's will?
What is the evidence that faith increases?

days.title: The Boundaries of Faith and the Shariah
days.question: What nullifies faith? And is the Shariah still suitable for our time?
days.principle: Faith is nullified by apostasy just as wudu is nullified by ritual impurity. Islam is a creed and a law suitable for every time and place, and anything introduced into the religion contrary to the Sunnah is rejected and returned to whoever introduced it.

misconception.peopleSay: The Shariah suited an old era and is not suitable for this age.
misconception.correct: The Shariah of Islam is suitable for every time and place; no new situation befalls anyone on earth without the Quran containing evidence of the way of guidance in it.

days.action: Before any act of worship today, ask yourself two questions: is it sincerely for Allah? And is it according to the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ?
lesson: The book says that faith is nullified by apostasy just as wudu is nullified by ritual impurity. Apostasy can be by leaving Islam entirely or by rejecting something Allah revealed after knowing it. When Iblis refused to obey and was arrogant, he nullified his faith, and whoever disbelieves without coercion deserves Allah's anger. Then the book establishes that Islam is a creed and a law suitable for every time and place; there is no new situation without the Quran containing evidence of guidance in it, either by explicit text or by referral to another proof. The Prophet ﷺ left us the Quran and the Sunnah and guaranteed that we would not go astray if we held fast to them. Anything done in the religion contrary to the Sunnah is rejected. The deed most beloved to Allah is the most sincere and the most correct.
days.quote: This clarification is of two kinds: clarification by explicit text, and clarification by referral to one of the other proofs the Lawgiver established in His Book as proofs and arguments for His creation.

quiz.question: Can a Muslim leave Islam after entering it?
options: Yes, faith is nullified by apostasy just as wudu is nullified by ritual impurity
No, whoever enters Islam never leaves
No, except by an official declaration
He leaves by any sin
quiz.explanation: We believe that faith is nullified by apostasy just as wudu is nullified by ritual impurity.

quiz.question: Someone invented a new act of worship with no basis in the Sunnah and says it brings him closer to Allah. What is its ruling?
options: Accepted if his intention is good
Recommended
Accepted if people do it
Rejected and returned to him

quiz.question: Someone says: "This Shariah was for a specific era." What is the correct understanding?
options: He is right
It suits acts of worship only
The Shariah is suitable for every time and place, and every new situation has guidance
It suits only the Arabs

askTheBook: What nullifies faith?
What does it mean that the Shariah is suitable for every time and place?
What is the ruling on innovation in the religion?

days.title: The Companions: The Best Generation
days.question: What is our position toward the Companions? And how do we deal with the disputes that happened between them?
days.principle: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ are the elite of this Ummah, their generation is the best of generations, and loving them is a sign of faith. So we bind our hearts to loving them, being pleased with them and refraining from what happened between them, without believing that any of them was infallible.

misconception.peopleSay: The Companions are infallible and never make mistakes.
misconception.correct: We bind our hearts to loving them, being pleased with them and refraining from what happened between them, without believing that any of them was infallible.

days.action: Supplicate today with the supplication in the verse of Surat al-Hashr: ﴿رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَٰنِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ﴾.
lesson: The Companions are the elite of this Ummah, their generation is the best of generations, and loving them is a sign of faith. Allah praised them in the Quran as firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves, and declared that He had turned to them in forgiveness and was pleased with them. He described the Emigrants with truthfulness and the Helpers with success, and the believers who came after them as praying for them with no rancour in their hearts. The Prophet ﷺ forbade insulting them, and said that if one of us spent the like of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach a single handful of theirs, nor half of it. So a Muslim loves them, is pleased with them, and holds his tongue about the disputes that happened between them. Even so, he does not believe that any of them was infallible.
days.quote: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade insulting them, and made clear that no one who came after them would reach their rank.

quiz.question: Someone insults a Companion. What is the ruling?
options: Fine if he has an opinion
Forbidden, because the Prophet ﷺ forbade insulting his Companions
Freedom of expression
Permissible if he read something negative about him
quiz.explanation: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade insulting them, and made clear that no one who came after them would reach their rank.

quiz.question: Are the Companions infallible?
options: No, we love them and are pleased with them without believing any of them was infallible
Yes, all of them are infallible
Only the senior ones are infallible
We don't have to love them because they aren't infallible
quiz.explanation: Without believing that any of them was infallible.

quiz.question: If someone today gave a mountain of gold in charity, would he reach the rank of a Companion?
options: Yes, and more
Yes, if his intention is pure
Possibly, if he does many deeds
No, he would not reach even half of the handful a Companion gave

askTheBook: What is our position on the disputes between the Companions?
What is the virtue of the Companions in the Quran?
What did the Prophet ﷺ say about insulting his Companions?

days.title: One Ummah, and Leadership
days.question: What unites Muslims even though their languages, countries and colours differ?
days.principle: Muslims are one Ummah; the foundation of this unity is gathering upon Islam and referring judgement to the pure Shariah. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim however different their tongues, colours and countries, and the supreme leadership (al-imamah al-'uzma) is among the greatest aims of the religion and its most emphasised obligations.

misconception.peopleSay: People are ranked by lineage, colour or country.
misconception.correct: Taqwa alone is the measure of superiority among people. The Prophet ﷺ said: «لا فضل لعربي على أعجمي ولا لأحمر على أسود إلا بالتقوى».

days.action: Notice today if you find yourself boasting of a family or country, or belittling someone because of their colour or origin, and remember that taqwa alone is the measure with Allah.
lesson: Allah said in the Quran that this Ummah is one Ummah and He is its Lord, so a Muslim in any country is the brother of a Muslim in any other. The Quran says the believers are brothers, and commands us to hold fast to the rope of Allah all together and not be divided. Superiority among people with Allah is by taqwa only, not by lineage or colour. The Prophet ﷺ called partisanship for a tribe or group a call of the Jahiliyyah, and when the Emigrants and Helpers called out to one another in partisanship, he said: leave it, for it is foul. Then the book establishes that the supreme leadership is among the greatest aims of the religion, because it stands in place of prophethood in guarding the religion and running worldly affairs by it. The Companions agreed it was obligatory after the Prophet's ﷺ death, because many obligations, such as establishing rulings and spreading security, cannot be fulfilled without it.
days.quote: This framework embraces all the people of the qiblah, as long as none of them falls into a clear nullifier of Islam.

quiz.question: What is the measure by which people are ranked with Allah?
options: Nationality and colour
Lineage and family
Taqwa only
Money and position
quiz.explanation: And He made clear that taqwa alone is the measure of superiority among people.

quiz.question: Someone showed partisanship for his country or tribe against other Muslims. What is the ruling?
options: Normal, it's natural belonging
The Prophet ﷺ said about such partisanship: leave it, for it is foul
Recommended
Permissible if he is in the right

quiz.question: Who is included within the framework of the Muslim Ummah?
options: All the people of the qiblah, as long as they do not fall into a clear nullifier of Islam
Only the followers of one school
Only the people of one country
Only the practising
quiz.explanation: This framework embraces all the people of the qiblah, as long as none of them falls into a clear nullifier of Islam.

askTheBook: What is the foundation of the unity of the Muslim Ummah?
What is a call of the Jahiliyyah?
Why is leadership (imamah) obligatory?

days.title: Sincere Advice, Obedience and the Community
days.question: What do those in authority have the right to from us? And why does Islam emphasise the community (al-jama'ah)?
days.principle: It is obligatory to give sincere advice to those in authority and to keep obeying them in what is not sinful, as long as they establish the Book of Allah in the Ummah. The community is mercy and division is punishment, and holding to the community is achieved by gathering upon the truth.

misconception.peopleSay: The community means the majority, so whatever most people do is the truth.
misconception.correct: The community, in the sense of following the truth, requires neither large nor small numbers; it is agreement with the truth, even if most people on earth oppose it.

days.action: If you have advice for someone responsible for you (at work, school or home), give it gently and kindly, as the book describes advising those in authority.
lesson: Among the rights of those in authority over us is that we advise them and obey them in what is not sinful, as long as they establish the Book of Allah in the Ummah. Advising them means helping them upon the truth, reminding them gently and kindly, and informing them of the rights of Muslims they have overlooked. The verse made obeying them obligatory, but not absolutely; it is within the limits of obeying Allah and His Messenger. Then the book establishes that the community is mercy and division is punishment. The community has two meanings: following the truth even if its people are few, and gathering around the Muslim ruler and obeying him in what is not sinful. Nu'aym ibn Hammad said that if the community becomes corrupt, hold to what it was upon before it became corrupt, even if you are alone.
days.quote: Because the truth is what the first community was upon, the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, regardless of how many people of falsehood come after them.

quiz.question: The person in authority ordered you to commit a sin. Do you obey him?
options: Yes, his obedience is absolute
Yes, and the sin is on him
Yes, if you are afraid
No, if he orders a sin, there is no hearing and no obeying

quiz.question: If most people abandoned the truth, where is the community then?
options: Always with the majority
There is no community then
The community is agreement with the truth, even if most people oppose it
With the strongest
quiz.explanation: In this sense it requires neither large nor small numbers; rather it is agreement with the truth, even if most people on earth oppose it.

quiz.question: To whom is sincere advice in the religion due?
options: Only to rulers
To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people
Only to the common people
Only to those we love

askTheBook: What are the rights of those in authority in Islam?
What does "the community is mercy and division is punishment" mean?
Does the community mean the majority?

days.title: The Path to Empowerment
days.question: How can the Ummah become strong again? And does jihad mean only fighting?
days.principle: Faith and jihad are the way to reviving this Ummah, achieving stewardship on earth and establishing the religion. Jihad is by striving to make oneself learn Allah's command, stay upright upon it, call to it, fight in His cause, and be patient with the trials that arise.

misconception.peopleSay: Jihad means fighting and nothing else; it has no other form.
misconception.correct: Jihad is by striving to make oneself learn Allah's command, stay upright upon it, call to it, fight in His cause and be patient with trials. The Prophet ﷺ said: «والمجاهد من جاهد نفسه في طاعة الله عز وجل».

days.action: Strive against yourself today in one thing: learn a matter of your religion, or stay consistent in an act of obedience you neglect, as the book counts these among the forms of jihad.
lesson: The book says that the way to revive the Ummah and establish the religion is faith and jihad. Jihad is broader than people think: making yourself learn Allah's command, staying upright upon it, calling to it, fighting in His cause, and being patient with trials. The Quran called faith and jihad the trade that saves from a painful punishment. Seeking knowledge is a type of jihad, and the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise. Abu ad-Darda' said that whoever does not see going out morning and evening for knowledge as jihad is lacking in intellect. Surat al-'Asr brings together the four types of jihad, so much so that al-Shafi'i said that had Allah revealed nothing but it, it would have sufficed people.
days.quote: That is why al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Had Allah revealed to His servants nothing but this surah, it would have sufficed them.

quiz.question: Someone says jihad is only fighting. What does the book say?
options: Jihad includes learning Allah's command, uprightness, calling to Islam, fighting and patience
He is right
Jihad is only calling to Islam
Jihad does not exist in this age
quiz.explanation: We believe that faith and jihad are the way…

quiz.question: Someone goes to the mosque to learn or teach something good. What is his reward?
options: No special reward
The reward of one prayer
The reward of a small charity
The reward of a mujahid

quiz.question: What is the path to the Ummah's revival and empowerment?
options: Material power only
Isolation from people
Faith, and jihad in its comprehensive meaning
Imitating other nations
quiz.explanation: Had Allah revealed to His servants nothing but this surah, it would have sufficed them.

askTheBook: What is the path to the Ummah's empowerment?
What are the forms of jihad in Islam?
Why does Surat al-'Asr bring together the types of jihad?
